sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a house in the City of St. Louis?
sections.html:
The City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue bills and collects real estate tax, and the city Assessor sets the value. St. Louis is an independent city, so there is no separate county treasurer to call. Both offices work from City Hall at 1200 Market Street.

The Collector's real estate tax page says the office collects on roughly 220,000 parcels inside city limits. It also says the Assessor revalues property every other year, in the odd-numbered years. The city's founding goes back to 1764, and in 1877 its voters separated it from St. Louis County, which is why the city runs both functions itself.

sections.h2: When is St. Louis property tax due and what is the penalty?
sections.html:
Tax is due by December 31, and the Collector mails notices every November. Anything unpaid on January 1 carries a one-time 2% penalty plus interest of 2% per month, capped at 18% per year, as set by Missouri law.

If your lender escrows your taxes, the bill goes to the lender. A bill that never arrives usually means the Assessor has an old mailing address, or the house changed hands after the bills were printed. All bills can be pulled up online, and a change of address goes through the Assessor's office in City Hall Room 114. Unpaid tax follows an order: if prior years are owed, the oldest year has to be paid first.

  • Online with a PayIt St. Louis account, through the web or a phone app.
  • In person at 1200 Market Street, Room 109, Monday through Friday, by card, cash, check, money order or cashier's check. No checks are accepted for delinquent payments.
  • By mail to Collector of Revenue, PO Box 66877, St. Louis, MO 63166-6877, with a check, money order or cashier's check.
  • By phone at (314) 408-6887 with a debit or credit card.

From mid-October through December 31 there is also a night deposit box at four Commerce Bank locations, according to the payment options page. The Collector also runs a pre-pay program for deposits toward future bills.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a St. Louis assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal hearing at the Assessor's office, then go to the Board of Equalization, then the State Tax Commission. The city's appeal page sets informal hearings from May 1 through June 23. Email appeal@stlouis-mo.gov with the parcel number or address, or leave a message at 314-622-4185.

Useful evidence includes a recent sales contract, an appraisal from a licensed appraiser, sales of comparable houses, and photographs of defects.

  1. Informal hearing with an appraiser, May 1 to June 23.
  2. Board of Equalization appeal placed with the Assessor by the second Monday in July. The board sits from July until the last Saturday in August, and the form comes from the Assessor or Room 120 at City Hall.
  3. State Tax Commission appeal, due by September 30 or 30 days after the board decides, whichever is later. A BOE appeal must come first, with limited exceptions such as newly purchased property.

A residential owner can speak for themselves before the Commission, while a commercial owner needs legal representation. State law helps the owner at the board level: RSMo 138.060 says there is no presumption the assessor's value is right, and in a city not within a county the assessor must prove the value does not exceed true market value. Anyone who pays the bill while disputing it should read RSMo 139.031 on paying under protest.

sections.h2: What happens to a St. Louis house when the tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After the January 1 delinquency, the city files a tax suit, and the sale takes place about a year later. The City's suit and sale schedule shows that Suit 245 was filed on October 13, 2026, with notices published weekly through November 10, 2026. The Sheriff's Office runs the sale itself.

An owner can settle a suit in full or ask the Collector about a Redemption Contract at 622-4101. Bids at the sale start at the amount in the legal description of the sale notice. Missouri's general statute, RSMo 140.150, requires the collector to mail notices to the record owner before delinquent land is published for sale, and says failing to receive the notice does not erase the debt.

sections.h2: Are there tax credits or exemptions for St. Louis owners?
sections.html:
Yes, with narrow eligibility. The Missouri Property Tax Credit Claim gives qualified seniors and people who are 100 percent disabled a credit toward real estate tax or rent paid. The city page puts the maximum at $1,100 for owners who live in their home and $750 for renters, with the amount based on taxes or rent paid and total household income. Call (573) 751-3505 for details.

Exempt status is separate. The Assessor decides it property by property, and the owner has to show proof that the use meets Article X, Section 6 of the Missouri Constitution and RSMo 137.100.

sections.h2: How big is St. Louis and who owns homes here?
sections.html:
The city covers 61.74 square miles of land and held 301,578 residents at the April 2020 census, down from 319,294 in 2010. The July 2025 estimate is 278,144, and the Census lists 4,885 people per square mile for 2020. Households average 1.92 people, and the Census counts 144,891 households.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,487, and owners without one report $574. Those figures help when you compare the tax bill on your parcel with what a buyer will carry each month. A bill that looks large next to those medians is a reason to review the assessment before the May 1 window opens.

sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in St. Louis with tax due?
sections.html:
Settle the balance at closing. The buyer's title company will search for liens, and tax that is delinquent or in suit has to be cleared or paid from the proceeds. Give the title company the parcel number early so it can request a payoff.

The Assessor's page also links to the Housing Conservation inspection for Residential Occupancy, described as a basic code inspection for minimal interior building code violations and minimum exterior standards. Ask the city whether that inspection applies to your sale.

faqs.q: Who do I pay St. Louis city real estate tax to?
faqs.a: The City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue, at 1200 Market Street, Room 109. You can also pay online through PayIt St. Louis, by mail to PO Box 66877, or by phone at (314) 408-6887.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in St. Louis?
faqs.a: A one-time 2% penalty plus 2% interest per month, up to 18% per year, on any balance left after December 31. Interest keeps accruing each year until the amount is paid in full.

faqs.q: When can I ask the Assessor to lower my value?
faqs.a: Informal hearings run May 1 through June 23. Email appeal@stlouis-mo.gov with your parcel number, or call 314-622-4185. The Board of Equalization deadline is the second Monday in July.

faqs.q: Is there a county treasurer for the city?
faqs.a: No. St. Louis is independent of any county, so the city Assessor and city Collector of Revenue fill the roles a county assessor and collector would elsewhere in Missouri.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house if tax is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and a payoff request through the title company shows the exact figure. If a tax suit has been filed, ask the Collector at 622-4101 about a Redemption Contract.
